Empirical order discovery reveals structured regularities only when actively searched, suggesting that cognition is not passive but purposefully structured. Pragmatic necessity motivates this search, aligning with the principle that knowledge must serve utility. Together, these primitives define a dual-process model: automatic associative learning and deliberate analytical reasoning. The failure mode occurs when associations mislead or when order is overlooked due to lack of motivation. In GSI, this manifests as overfitting to spurious correlations; in GSE, as rigid adherence to outdated strategies. The epistemic lens thus unifies perception, inference, and action into a coherent framework of situated intelligence.
